hypothesis: Explicit register storage hints might preserve macro-expanded scalar lifetimes and cause GC/1.3 to allocate the retail nonvolatile FPR set f14-f31.
hypothesis_result: The register-qualified honest C emitted byte-identical code to the preserved candidate: 51.559734%, 1404 bytes, a 0x60-byte frame, and f27-f31 only. A separately measured exact-small-data/signed-table plus array-interval variant corrected several early SDA21 and lhax forms but regressed to 50.402657% and 1392 bytes, so it was not preserved.
divergence: Retail saves f14-f31 in a 0x160-byte frame and spills plane distances, products, and the normalized normal; the candidate saves only f27-f31 in a 0x60-byte frame. Expression scheduling differs throughout the plane and interval calculations, and 8 relocation-bearing instructions remain absent or different.
